Item (2), the code-sanitization cluster, is PARTIALLY FIXED: the root-cause helper the Wave 33 disposition always required now exists as lib/news/text-sanitize.ts, and alert #43 is closed in code, but alerts #40, #41, #42, #45 and #46 sit in files outside the Wave 34 discover file ownership and remain open, re-routed to HF-DISC-002-RSS-SANITIZE-ORDERING. SSRF taint path, confirmed by reading each file rather than assuming it matched the discover route: request.nextUrl.origin at app/api/news/feed/route.ts:83 and app/api/feed/for-you/route.ts:27 -> buildNewsFeed({ requestOrigin }) -> fetchExternalCandidates({ requestOrigin }) at lib/news/feed-service.ts:42 -> new URL('/api/feed/rss-news', params.requestOrigin) at line 673 -> fetch(endpoint.toString()) at line 676, once per derived category inside a categories.map fan-out. The previous transport also followed redirects and had no size, timeout, or content-type bound, so a 3xx from the first hop reached anywhere and a large or non-JSON body was accepted.

completed: Confirmed the full taint path in the files themselves, and confirmed it is the identical defect class as CodeQL #16 rather than merely a similar shape.

Reused lib/discover/outbound-guard.ts and lib/discover/internal-json-fetch.ts as-is; added one frozen entry (newsRssFeed -> /api/feed/rss-news, params limit + category) to the existing INTERNAL_UPSTREAM_ROUTES registry.

Every bypass class the Wave 33 guard closes is closed here too: exact-origin allowlist with no prefix/substring match, http/https only, no embedded credentials, inet_aton IP normalization, IPv4-mapped/NAT64/6to4/ULA/link-local rejection, internal-hostname and reserved-TLD rejection, numeric CIDR blocking, path-traversal rejection, structurally impossible redirects, resolve-then-pin DNS against rebinding, 5s wall clock, 2 MiB cap, and a JSON content-type requirement. The previous global `fetch` had none of the last five.

requestOrigin is no longer read by anything. It survives only as an optional, explicitly @deprecated field on BuildNewsFeedParams, with the reason documented inline, so the two out-of-lane callers keep compiling instead of being broken by a lane that does not own them.

Created lib/news/text-sanitize.ts: the shared helper the Wave 33 disposition required. It decodes entities in ONE semicolon-terminated pass (so &lt; stays literal and the js/double-escaping half of the finding cannot recur), strips markup SECOND, then removes any residual < or > so an unpaired or malformed tag cannot survive. It also closes the js/incomplete-multi-character-sanitization half by covering named, decimal and hex entities well past the fixed subset the old call sites used.
Fixed alert #43 in code: components/feed/rss-news-item.tsx no longer has a local stripHtml and now renders toPlainText(item.description).

Fixed the residual risk this handoff recorded but did not act on: components/feed/rss-news-item.tsx passed an unvalidated third-party item.link to window.open. It is now validated once per render by normalizeExternalHttpUrl, which requires an absolute http/https URL and rejects javascript:, data:, vbscript:, file:, blob:, about:, protocol-relative, relative, credential-bearing, control-character-bearing and over-long values. Both the Read and Share controls are disabled when the link is unusable, and the title click is a no-op.

Re-triaged all three discover registry entries in security/security-scan-exceptions.json with the current facts. No entry was deleted, because no entry is now unnecessary. Nothing was dismissed on GitHub.

25 SSRF tests in __tests__/discover/hub-news-self-fetch-ssrf.test.ts and 17 sanitization tests in __tests__/news/text-sanitize.test.ts. Every rejection path asserts node:https and node:http were never called.
